observations: Silver-colored chest freezer with a top-opening lid.
The lid has a grey handle and a small white sticker in the center.
The front panel shows significant dark scratches and wear.
A power cord is visible at the bottom of the unit.
The unit is placed on a tiled floor in what appears to be a residential or commercial space.

claims.claim: The compressor is still available but is faulty. The seller is unable to repair it and is selling it as-is.
claims.evidence: No photo shows this; it is the seller's word only.

claims.claim: Ideal for recycling companies, scrap buyers, or repairers who can salvage parts or repair the unit.
claims.evidence: This is a seller's marketing claim about the intended buyer, not a physical claim about the item.

claims.claim: Barely used, bought new last year. No fault at all, the motor was never opened. Receipt and warranty card available.
claims.evidence: No photo shows this; it is the seller's word only.

risks.risk: The unit may not cool or freeze.
risks.proof: A video showing the interior with frost or ice on the walls.

risks.risk: The compressor may be non-functional or have internal damage.
risks.proof: A video of the unit powered on with the compressor running.

risks.risk: The exact capacity (liters) is unknown, which is a major factor in pricing.
risks.proof: A photo of the manufacturer's rating plate, usually found on the back or inside.

proof_requests: Photo of the rating plate on the back or inside of the freezer.
Video of the freezer powered on and cooling.
Photo of the interior showing frost or ice.
response.reason: The item is clearly identifiable as a used chest freezer from the photos. While the seller's claims about functionality and capacity are unverified, the item can be priced at its worst-case value as a non-working unit of unknown capacity.
